newsitem.title: GERMANY: TENNIS-GRAF STRETCHED AFTER INJURY ABSENCE.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-GRAF STRETCHED AFTER INJURY ABSENCE.

text.p: Steffi Graf, playing her first match after three months out with a knee injury, struggled to a three-set win over American Chanda Rubin at the German Open on Tuesday.
Graf, who lost her world number one ranking to Swiss Martina Hingis in March and is seeking her 10th Berlin title, triumphed 6-3 3-6 6-1.
But she was slow to get into the match, losing two service games to love in the first set but benefited from dozens of unforced errors by her opponent.

The top seed appeared visibly stunned at losing the second set as Rubin, unseeded and ranked 27th in the world, broke Graf's consistently fragile service in the eighth game and then held her own to square the match.

But with a menacing glare Graf rattled off the first four games of the decider, as Rubin's service became even more unreliable then her own, to demonstrate that a return to full fitness may not be far off.

"I felt very uncertain out there at first," Graf said. "I gave away a lot of easy points. I wasn't in the shape that I would like to be. I am not very happy with my performance, but happy that I made it through my first match."
It was Graf's sixth win in six matches against Rubin, who climbed as high as sixth in the world rankings in 1996 before an injury to her playing hand forced a long lay-off.
Graf had received a bye into the second round and now meets 15th seed Ruxandra Dragomir of Romania, a finalist at the Hamburg Open earlier this month.

Newly-crowned Italian Open champion Mary Pierce of France, seeded 12th, maintained her form. She brushed aside Germany's Elena Wagner 6-2 6-3 to set up a second round tie against Slovakian ninth seed Karina Habsudova.
But Spain's world number six Arantxa Sanchez Vicario had to fight to overcome Austria's Barbara Schett 6-2 4-6 7-5.
